symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC2, also supposed to be in VLAN 10, but both get valid IPs from DHCP.
topology_note: Both PCs connect to SW1, access ports Fa0/2 and Fa0/4.
show_output:
SW1#show vlan brief
VLAN Name        Status   Ports
10   Sales       active   Fa0/2
20   Engineering active   Fa0/4, Fa0/5
expected_fault: Fa0/4 was assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10 - PCs are on different VLANs despite same subnet config.

symptom: PCs on VLAN 30 cannot reach the file server on VLAN 30, but ping their own default gateway fine.
topology_note: SW1 trunk to SW2 carries traffic to distribution switch; server sits on SW2.
show_output:
SW1#show interfaces trunk
Port     Mode   Encapsulation  Status       Native vlan
Gi0/1    on     802.1q         trunking     1

Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Port     Vlans allowed
Gi0/1    1,10,20
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is not permitted on the trunk link (allowed list only has 1,10,20), so VLAN 30 traffic is dropped between switches.

symptom: New PC plugged into Fa0/6 gets no DHCP address at all.
topology_note: Fa0/6 should be an access port on VLAN 10 like the rest of the sales floor.
show_output:
SW1#show interfaces Fa0/6 switchport
Name: Fa0/6
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: down
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Port is still on default VLAN 1 and never manually configured for VLAN 10, so it's not reaching the correct DHCP scope.

symptom: Two PCs in the same VLAN can't ping each other even though switchport shows correct VLAN.
topology_note: Both connect through the same switch, different ports.
show_output:
SW1#show mac address-table | include 000C
  10   000C.29F1.22A1  DYNAMIC  Fa0/2
  10   000C.29F1.22A1  DYNAMIC  Fa0/4
expected_fault: Duplicate MAC address appearing on two ports (likely a cloned VM NIC or spoofing) causing MAC flapping.

symptom: PC has a valid IP but cannot ping its own default gateway.
topology_note: PC1 on 192.168.10.0/24, gateway is router sub-interface.
show_output:
PC1> ipconfig
IP: 192.168.10.50  Mask: 255.255.255.0  Gateway: 192.168.10.1

R1#show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0.10   192.168.20.1   up   up
expected_fault: Gateway configured on the router (192.168.20.1) doesn't match the subnet the PC expects (192.168.10.x).

symptom: PC can ping default gateway but nothing beyond it.
topology_note: R1 connects to ISP router via Gi0/1.
show_output:
R1#show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/1   203.0.113.2   administratively down   down
expected_fault: Uplink interface is administratively shut down.

symptom: Gateway ping works intermittently, sometimes times out.
topology_note: PC connected via a long Cat5 run to closet switch.
show_output:
SW1#show interfaces Fa0/8
Fa0/8 is up, line protocol is up (looped back)
  5000 input errors, 3000 CRC, 0 collisions
expected_fault: High CRC/input errors indicate a bad cable or duplex mismatch causing intermittent packet loss.

symptom: New VLAN's PCs can't reach their gateway even though the SVI is configured.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick setup with sub-interfaces.
show_output:
R1#show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0.30   192.168.30.1   up   down
expected_fault: Sub-interface protocol is down - likely missing 'encapsulation dot1Q 30' command, so it can't process tagged frames.

symptom: Several PCs on VLAN 10 get 169.254.x.x addresses (APIPA).
topology_note: DHCP server is a Cisco router with 'ip dhcp pool SALES'.
show_output:
R1#show ip dhcp pool SALES
Pool SALES:
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Total addresses                : 10
 Leased addresses               : 10
expected_fault: DHCP scope for VLAN 10 is exhausted (all 10 addresses leased out), so new clients fail to get an IP.

symptom: PCs on VLAN 20 (a different subnet than the router) get no DHCP address at all.
topology_note: DHCP server lives centrally on R1; VLAN 20 clients are behind SW2 with an SVI on a different router.
show_output:
R2#show run interface vlan20
interface Vlan20
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
! no ip helper-address configured
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 20 SVI, so DHCP broadcast requests never reach the remote DHCP server.

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN end up with identical IP addresses, causing intermittent connectivity for both.
topology_note: One PC has a static IP configured inside the DHCP pool's range.
show_output:
R1#show ip dhcp conflict
IP address       Detection method   Detection time
192.168.10.55    Ping               10:15 UTC
expected_fault: A statically assigned PC is using an address inside the active DHCP pool range, causing an IP conflict.

symptom: All DHCP requests on VLAN 10 fail after a config change on the switch.
topology_note: SW1 recently had DHCP snooping enabled for security.
show_output:
SW1#show ip dhcp snooping
Switch DHCP snooping is enabled
Interface       Trusted
Gi0/1           no
expected_fault: Uplink port toward the DHCP server is not marked as a trusted port under DHCP snooping, so legitimate server replies are being dropped.

symptom: PC can ping the web server's IP directly but browsing by hostname fails.
topology_note: PC uses DHCP-assigned DNS server.
show_output:
PC1> ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 192.168.100.53

PC1> ping 192.168.100.53
Request timed out.
expected_fault: Configured DNS server is unreachable - likely wrong DNS IP handed out by DHCP or DNS server is down.

symptom: Internal hostnames resolve fine, but external websites don't.
topology_note: Internal DNS server forwards unknown queries upstream.
show_output:
DNS1#show run | include forwarder
! no forwarder configured
expected_fault: Internal DNS server has no forwarder set for external queries, so it can't resolve anything outside its own zone.

symptom: All name resolution fails network-wide, users report 'server not found' for everything.
topology_note: DNS server VM is hosted on VLAN 100.
show_output:
R1#show ip interface brief
Vlan100   192.168.100.1   up   up

PC1> ping 192.168.100.53
Reply from 192.168.100.1: Destination host unreachable
expected_fault: DNS server itself is powered off or its NIC is down - no route exists to reach it even though the gateway is fine.

symptom: DNS resolution works from PCs but fails from a specific VLAN (Guest).
topology_note: ACL was recently applied restricting Guest VLAN traffic.
show_output:
R1#show access-lists GUEST_ACL
10 deny udp 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 53
20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL explicitly blocks UDP port 53 (DNS) from the Guest subnet.

symptom: PCs on VLAN 10 can reach VLAN 20 but not the remote branch office subnet.
topology_note: R1 connects to branch via a WAN link using OSPF.
show_output:
R1#show ip route
O    10.20.0.0/24 [110/20] via 172.16.0.2, 00:00:12, Serial0/0/0
! Expected route to 10.30.0.0/24 (branch) missing
expected_fault: No route to the branch subnet (10.30.0.0/24) - likely OSPF neighbor down or network statement missing on branch router.

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing stopped working after router reload.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick with sub-interfaces for VLAN 10/20/30.
show_output:
R1#show run | include interface
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
! sub-interface for VLAN 30 missing after reload - config not saved
expected_fault: Running-config was never saved to startup-config, so the VLAN 30 sub-interface was lost on reload.

symptom: Static route to a remote subnet was added, but traffic still fails.
show_output:
R1#show ip route static
S    10.40.0.0/24 [1/0] via 10.1.1.2

R1#ping 10.1.1.2
Success rate is 0 percent
expected_fault: Static route points to a next-hop IP that is itself unreachable - likely wrong next-hop or that interface is down.

symptom: Traffic to the internet works, but return traffic never arrives back at internal PCs.
topology_note: Asymmetric routing suspected - two WAN links to different ISPs.
show_output:
R1#show ip route 0.0.0.0
S*   0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1
! But NAT is applied on the other interface toward 198.51.100.1
expected_fault: Default route and NAT outside interface don't match - traffic goes out one ISP link but NAT/PAT is configured for the other, causing asymmetric routing.

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 can ping the server but cannot open a web page hosted on it.
topology_note: ACL applied on R1's inbound interface for VLAN 10.
show_output:
R1#show access-lists 101
10 permit icmp any any
20 deny tcp any any eq 80
30 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies TCP port 80 (HTTP) while allowing ICMP, explaining why ping works but web browsing doesn't.

symptom: After applying a new ACL, ALL traffic from VLAN 20 stopped, including traffic that should be allowed.
topology_note: ACL was applied to interface but has no explicit permit statements besides one line.
show_output:
R1#show access-lists 102
10 permit tcp 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 443
! No other permit lines - implicit deny any any
expected_fault: Missing explicit 'permit ip any any' (or similar) at the end - the implicit deny-all at the end of every ACL is blocking everything else.
concept_tag: Implicit deny at end of ACL

symptom: ACL meant to block one specific host is blocking the whole subnet instead.
topology_note: Admin intended to block only 192.168.10.50.
show_output:
R1#show access-lists 103
10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any
20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: Wildcard mask used denies the entire /24 subnet (0.0.0.255) instead of a single host (should be 0.0.0.0 for a host statement).

symptom: ACL was configured correctly but has no effect on traffic at all.
topology_note: ACL 104 written and verified in running-config.
show_output:
R1#show ip interface Gi0/1 | include access list
  Outgoing access list is not set
  Inbound  access list is not set
expected_fault: The ACL exists in config but was never actually applied to an interface with 'ip access-group'.

symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the internet even though the default route is correct.
topology_note: R1 configured with NAT overload (PAT) toward ISP.
show_output:
R1#show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 0
Outside interfaces: (none)
Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/0
expected_fault: No outside interface has been marked with 'ip nat outside', so NAT never triggers even though inside is configured.

symptom: Some internal PCs can reach the internet, others (same subnet) can't.
topology_note: NAT pool has limited addresses.
show_output:
R1#show ip nat translations
! Pool exhausted - 20/20 addresses in use

R1#show ip nat statistics
Pool NATPOOL: netmask 255.255.255.248
 start 203.0.113.10 end 203.0.113.13
 total addresses 4, allocated 4 (100%), misses 15
expected_fault: NAT pool is too small (only 4 public addresses) for the number of simultaneous internal users, causing PAT/pool exhaustion.

symptom: Web server behind NAT is unreachable from outside despite port forwarding being configured.
topology_note: Static NAT/PAT rule for port 80 forwarding to internal server.
show_output:
R1#show run | include ip nat inside source static
ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.10.100 8080 203.0.113.5 80 extendable
! Server actually listens on port 80, not 8080
expected_fault: Port forward maps to internal port 8080 but the web server actually listens on port 80, mismatching the internal port.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi devices can reach the internet but can also reach internal file servers (should be isolated).
topology_note: Guest SSID mapped to VLAN 40, internal servers on VLAN 10.
show_output:
R1#show access-lists GUEST_ISOLATION
! ACL exists but not applied to Vlan40 interface
expected_fault: Guest isolation ACL was created but never applied to the Guest VLAN interface - a security issue, not just connectivity.

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but never get an IP address.
topology_note: WLC bridges wireless VLAN 50 to wired network via trunk to core switch.
show_output:
CoreSW#show interfaces trunk
Port     Vlans allowed
Gi0/2    1,10,20,30
! VLAN 50 missing from allowed list
expected_fault: VLAN 50 (wireless) is not permitted on the trunk between WLC and core switch, so DHCP/data never reaches wireless clients.

symptom: Wireless clients can't authenticate to the SSID at all, get 'incorrect password' even with correct credentials.
topology_note: WPA2-Enterprise with RADIUS authentication.
show_output:
WLC#show radius statistics
Server 192.168.100.10: Requests 50, Timeouts 50, Responses 0
expected_fault: RADIUS server is unreachable or down, so no authentication requests are ever being answered.
